What if 90% of your best performing content was never meant to be original? Matt Espinoza runs Clover Labs, a company that went from zero to 8 million a year in six months and now does a quarter of a billion views a month for OpusClip, Superwall and Typing.com. He breaks down the new app content strategy dominating in 2026, and it has nothing to do with making new content. It is cloning what already works, at scale, on autopilot.

Cloning is 90% of every campaign they run. A clone does a median 20% of the original views, so five to ten of them match the original, and some do two to six times better. He clones a competitor slideshow in one click, splits a viral video into a hook and a demo to swap in his own product, then mass creates accounts across 20 countries and dubs the video into German for a 20% view lift. We also get into AI search, where his team does 150 million views from Reddit and blogs. He tests 2,000 prompts, estimates LLM volume at 30% of Google search, finds the threads ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews cite, and takes those spots with post seeding and comment seeding.
